rules.rule_name: Program Initialization - Capture Current Date as Submission Period
rules.rule_description: At the start of the monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract process, the system captures today's date in Julian format (YYDDD) to be used as the submission period identifier throughout the extract run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 1: Program Initialization - Capture current date as Julian format YYDDD as submission period identifier

acceptance_criteria.Given: The monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The program starts execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: Today's date is captured in Julian format (YYDDD) and stored as the submission period identifier to be used for all provider records written during this extract run

rules.rule_name: Julian Date Decomposition into Year and Day Components
rules.rule_description: The captured Julian date (YYDDD) is decomposed into two separate components: a 2-digit year (YY) and a 3-digit day-of-year (DDD), which are used independently in downstream validation and output population steps.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 2: Julian Date Decomposition - Break down Julian date into Year YY and Day-of-Year DDD components

acceptance_criteria.Given: Today's date has been captured in Julian format (YYDDD)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Julian date is decomposed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first 2 characters of the Julian date are extracted and stored as the current 2-digit year (YY), and the remaining 3 characters are extracted and stored as the current day-of-year (DDD)

rules.rule_name: Sequential Read of Provider Master File
rules.rule_description: The system reads provider records one at a time sequentially from the Provider Master File. This process continues in a loop until all records have been processed or the end of the file is reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 3: Provider Master File Sequential Read - Read next provider record from Provider Master file

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Provider Master File is open and available for reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The system requests the next provider record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next sequential provider record is retrieved from the Provider Master File for processing; if no more records exist, the end-of-file condition is set to true and the extraction loop terminates

rules.rule_name: Active Provider Filtering - Exclude Inactive Providers
rules.rule_description: Only providers whose status is marked as Active in the Provider Master File are eligible for inclusion in the T-MSIS submission. Providers with any other status are skipped and not written to the output file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 4: Active Provider Filtering - Is provider status Active?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File
acceptance_criteria.When: The provider's active status flag is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the provider is marked as Active, the record proceeds to enrollment date validation and T-MSIS output processing; if the provider is not Active (inactive), the record is skipped entirely and the system reads the next provider record without writing any output

rules.rule_name: Enrollment Date Future-Year Validation
rules.rule_description: For each active provider, the 2-digit year portion of the provider's enrollment effective date is extracted and compared against the current 2-digit year to detect potential future-dated enrollment records that may indicate a data quality issue.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 5: Enrollment Date Future-Year Validation - Extract 2-digit year from enrollment date and compare to current year

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider record has been identified as Active
acceptance_criteria.When: The enrollment effective date is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The 2-digit year is extracted from positions 3 and 4 of the provider's enrollment effective date field and compared to the current 2-digit year (YY) captured at program initialization

rules.rule_name: Future Enrollment Year Alert - Data Quality Warning
rules.rule_description: When an active provider's enrollment effective year is greater than the current year, a data quality warning is raised identifying the provider by their NPI. The warning does not prevent the record from being written to the T-MSIS output file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 6: Future Enrollment Alert - Display warning message with NPI flagging potential data quality issue

acceptance_criteria.Given: An active provider's enrollment effective year has been extracted and compared to the current year
acceptance_criteria.When: The enrollment effective year is greater than the current 2-digit year
acceptance_criteria.Then: A warning message 'PRVTMS01: FUTURE ENROLLMENT? NPI [provider NPI]' is displayed to flag the potential data quality issue, and processing continues — the provider record is still written to the T-MSIS output file

rules.rule_name: Provider Medicaid ID Mapping to T-MSIS Output Record
rules.rule_description: The provider's Medicaid ID from the Provider Master File is mapped directly into the Provider ID field of the T-MSIS output record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 7: Provider Medicaid ID Mapping - Copy Medicaid ID into T-MSIS output record

acceptance_criteria.Given: An active provider record is being prepared for T-MSIS output
acceptance_criteria.When: The Provider ID field of the T-MSIS output record is populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Medicaid ID value from the Provider Master File record is copied exactly into the Provider ID field of the T-MSIS output record

rules.rule_name: Provider NPI Mapping to T-MSIS Output Record
rules.rule_description: The provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) from the Provider Master File is mapped directly into the NPI field of the T-MSIS output record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 8: Provider NPI Mapping - Copy NPI into T-MSIS output record

acceptance_criteria.Given: An active provider record is being prepared for T-MSIS output
acceptance_criteria.When: The NPI field of the T-MSIS output record is populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The NPI value from the Provider Master File record is copied exactly into the NPI field of the T-MSIS output record

rules.rule_name: Provider Active Status Assignment in T-MSIS Output
rules.rule_description: All providers written to the T-MSIS output file are assigned a status of 'A' (Active), reflecting that only active providers are included in the T-MSIS submission.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 9: Provider Active Status Assignment - Set status field to A Active in T-MSIS output record

acceptance_criteria.Given: An active provider record is being prepared for T-MSIS output
acceptance_criteria.When: The status field of the T-MSIS output record is populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The status field in the T-MSIS output record is set to the fixed value 'A', representing Active status

rules.rule_name: Submission Period Assignment Using Today's Julian Date
rules.rule_description: The reporting period field in the T-MSIS output record is populated with today's Julian date (YYDDD), ensuring each provider record is associated with the correct submission period for the extract run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 10: Submission Period Assignment - Populate reporting period field with today's Julian date YYDDD

acceptance_criteria.Given: An active provider record is being prepared for T-MSIS output
acceptance_criteria.When: The reporting period field of the T-MSIS output record is populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: Today's Julian date (YYDDD), captured at program initialization, is copied into the reporting period field of the T-MSIS output record

rules.rule_name: T-MSIS Provider Record Assembly and Formatting
rules.rule_description: All individually mapped fields — Provider ID (Medicaid ID), NPI, Active Status ('A'), and Reporting Period (Julian date) — are assembled together into a complete, formatted T-MSIS provider output record ready for writing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 11: T-MSIS Record Formatting - Assemble complete T-MSIS record with type PRV01 provider ID NPI status and period

acceptance_criteria.Given: All individual T-MSIS output fields have been populated for an active provider
acceptance_criteria.When: The complete T-MSIS record is assembled
acceptance_criteria.Then: The fully populated T-MSIS detail record — containing Provider ID, NPI, Status 'A', and Reporting Period — is assembled into the T-MSIS output record structure ready for writing to the output file

rules.rule_name: T-MSIS Output Record Writing to Submission File
rules.rule_description: The fully assembled and formatted T-MSIS provider record is written to the T-MSIS Provider Submission output file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 12: T-MSIS Output Record Writing - Write formatted provider record to T-MSIS Provider Submission output file

acceptance_criteria.Given: A complete T-MSIS provider record has been assembled with all required fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The record is submitted to the T-MSIS output file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted T-MSIS provider record is written as a new record to the T-MSIS Provider Submission output file

rules.rule_name: Extracted Record Count Tracking
rules.rule_description: Each time a provider record is successfully written to the T-MSIS output file, a running counter is incremented by 1 to track the total number of provider records included in the submission.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 13: Extracted Record Count Tracking - Increment running counter for successfully written records

acceptance_criteria.Given: A T-MSIS provider record has been successfully written to the output file
acceptance_criteria.When: The record write operation completes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The running total count of successfully written T-MSIS provider records is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Extraction Summary Reporting at Process Completion
rules.rule_description: Upon completion of all record processing, the system displays a summary message showing the total number of provider rows written to the T-MSIS submission file during the extract run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 14: Extraction Summary Reporting - Display total provider rows written to T-MSIS submission file

acceptance_criteria.Given: All records in the Provider Master File have been processed and the end-of-file condition has been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The extraction loop terminates
acceptance_criteria.Then: A summary message 'PRVTMS01: T-MSIS PROVIDER ROWS= [count]' is displayed, reporting the total number of provider records successfully written to the T-MSIS output file

rules.rule_name: File Closure and Process Completion
rules.rule_description: After the extraction summary is reported, both the Provider Master File and the T-MSIS output file are closed, and the monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract process is completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 15: File Closure and Process Completion - Close Provider Master and T-MSIS output files

acceptance_criteria.Given: The extraction summary has been displayed and all provider records have been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program finalizes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Provider Master File and the T-MSIS Provider Submission output file are both closed, and the monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract process terminates successfully

rules.rule_name: Capture Today's Date in Julian Format for Enrollment Validation
rules.rule_description: The system obtains today's date in Julian format (YYDDD), where the first two digits represent the 2-digit year and the last three digits represent the day-of-year. This date is used as the reference point for all subsequent enrollment date validations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Then: Today's date is captured and stored in Julian format (YYDDD), where the 5-character value represents a 2-digit year followed by a 3-digit day-of-year (e.g., 25143 = Year 25, Day 143), and this value is made available for enrollment year and day-of-year comparisons

rules.rule_name: Extract Current Year Component from Julian Date
rules.rule_description: The system isolates the 2-digit year portion from the 5-character Julian date by reading the first two characters. This current year value is stored separately and used to detect future enrollment effective dates on provider records.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system decomposes the Julian date
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first 2 characters (positions 1–2) of the Julian date are extracted and stored as the Current Year (YY) component (e.g., from '25143', the value '25' is stored as the current year for use in enrollment year comparison)

rules.rule_name: Extract Current Day-of-Year Component from Julian Date
rules.rule_description: The system isolates the 3-digit day-of-year portion from the 5-character Julian date by reading the last three characters. This day-of-year value is stored separately and is available for enrollment age or period-based validations.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The last 3 characters (positions 3–5) of the Julian date are extracted and stored as the Current Day-of-Year (DDD) component (e.g., from '25143', the value '143' is stored as the current day-of-year for use in enrollment period validation)

rules.rule_name: Store Current Year for Provider Enrollment Year Comparison
rules.rule_description: The extracted 2-digit current year (YY) is retained in the system's working storage so that it can be compared against the enrollment effective year on each active provider record to identify future-dated enrollments.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

for Enrollment Year Comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The 2-digit current year (YY) has been extracted from today's Julian date
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the current year component
acceptance_criteria.Then: The 2-digit current year value (YY) is stored and remains available throughout the entire provider record processing loop, so that each active provider's enrollment effective year can be compared against it to detect future enrollment dates

rules.rule_name: Store Current Day-of-Year for Enrollment Period Stamping
rules.rule_description: The extracted 3-digit day-of-year (DDD) is retained in the system's working storage. Together with the current year (YY), the full Julian date (YYDDD) is used to stamp the reporting period on every T-MSIS provider output record.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the day-of-year component

rules.rule_name: Initialize Provider File Processing State
rules.rule_description: Before reading any provider records, the system must initialize the processing state to indicate that records are still available for processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Initialize End-of-File Flag to Not Reached

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Provider Master File sequential read process is about to begin
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the Provider Master File read loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to 'N' (Not Reached), indicating that provider records are available and processing should continue

rules.rule_name: Read Next Provider Record Sequentially
rules.rule_description: The system must read provider records one at a time in sequential order from the Provider Master File to ensure every provider record is evaluated for T-MSIS reporting.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Provider Master File is open for input and the End-of-File flag is set to 'Not Reached'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system requests the next record from the Provider Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next sequential provider record is retrieved from the Provider Master File and made available for processing

rules.rule_name: Detect End of Provider Master File
rules.rule_description: After each read attempt from the Provider Master File, the system must check whether all records have been processed to determine if the read loop should continue or terminate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End of File Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read attempt has been made on the Provider Master File
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the file status returned after the read operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status indicates End-of-File (no more records exist), the system marks all records as processed and exits the read loop; if the file status indicates a record was successfully retrieved, the provider record is made available for further processing and the loop continues

rules.rule_name: Mark All Provider Records as Processed
rules.rule_description: When no more provider records exist in the Provider Master File, the system must formally mark the processing as complete to stop further read attempts.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark All Records as Processed - Set End-of-File Flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read attempt on the Provider Master File has returned an End-of-File condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects that no more provider records are available
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to TRUE, signaling that all provider records have been processed and the sequential read loop should terminate

rules.rule_name: Continue Processing Available Provider Record
rules.rule_description: When a provider record is successfully retrieved from the Provider Master File, it must be passed forward for business evaluation and potential inclusion in the T-MSIS output.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Provider Record Available for Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read attempt on the Provider Master File has successfully retrieved a provider record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the record is available (no End-of-File condition)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The retrieved provider record is made available for downstream business processing, and the system loops back to read the next record after processing is complete

rules.rule_name: Active Provider Selection for T-MSIS Extraction
rules.rule_description: Determines whether a provider record from the Provider Master File should be included in the T-MSIS extract based on the provider's active status. Only providers with an Active status are selected for further processing and output; all others are skipped.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File
acceptance_criteria.When: The provider's status in the Provider Master File is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the provider status is marked as Active, the provider record is selected and processed for T-MSIS extraction; if the provider status is not marked as Active, the provider record is skipped and no further action is taken for that record

rules.rule_name: Include Active Provider in T-MSIS Output

acceptance_criteria.Then: The provider record is skipped entirely — no T-MSIS output record is created, no warning message is generated, and the output record counter is not incremented; processing continues with the next provider record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization - Capture Current Date as Submission Period
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of the monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract process, the system captures today's date in Julian format (YYDDD) to be used as the submission period identifier throughout the extract run.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Julian Date Decomposition into Year and Day Components
all_rules.Rule_Description: The captured Julian date (YYDDD) is decomposed into two separate components: a 2-digit year (YY) and a 3-digit day-of-year (DDD), which are used independently in downstream validation and output population steps.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Read of Provider Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads provider records one at a time sequentially from the Provider Master File. This process continues in a loop until all records have been processed or the end of the file is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provider's active status flag is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the provider is marked as Active, the record proceeds to enrollment date validation and T-MSIS output processing; if the provider is not Active (inactive), the record is skipped entirely and the system reads the next provider record without writing any output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Active Provider Filtering - Exclude Inactive Providers
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only providers whose status is marked as Active in the Provider Master File are eligible for inclusion in the T-MSIS submission. Providers with any other status are skipped and not written to the output file.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enrollment Date Future-Year Validation

Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Today's Julian date (YYDDD), captured at program initialization, is copied into the reporting period field of the T-MSIS output record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Submission Period Assignment Using Today's Julian Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The reporting period field in the T-MSIS output record is populated with today's Julian date (YYDDD), ensuring each provider record is associated with the correct submission period for the extract run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All individual T-MSIS output fields have been populated for an active provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The complete T-MSIS record is assembled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The fully populated T-MSIS detail record — containing Provider ID, NPI, Status 'A', and Reporting Period — is assembled into the T-MSIS output record structure ready for writing to the output file

all_rules.Rule_Name: T-MSIS Provider Record Assembly and Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: All individually mapped fields — Provider ID (Medicaid ID), NPI, Active Status ('A'), and Reporting Period (Julian date) — are assembled together into a complete, formatted T-MSIS provider output record ready for writing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A complete T-MSIS provider record has been assembled with all required fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record is submitted to the T-MSIS output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted T-MSIS provider record is written as a new record to the T-MSIS Provider Submission output file

all_rules.Rule_Name: T-MSIS Output Record Writing to Submission File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully assembled and formatted T-MSIS provider record is written to the T-MSIS Provider Submission output file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A T-MSIS provider record has been successfully written to the output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record write operation completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The running total count of successfully written T-MSIS provider records is incremented by 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extracted Record Count Tracking
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each time a provider record is successfully written to the T-MSIS output file, a running counter is incremented by 1 to track the total number of provider records included in the submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All records in the Provider Master File have been processed and the end-of-file condition has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The extraction loop terminates
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A summary message 'PRVTMS01: T-MSIS PROVIDER ROWS= [count]' is displayed, reporting the total number of provider records successfully written to the T-MSIS output file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extraction Summary Reporting at Process Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon completion of all record processing, the system displays a summary message showing the total number of provider rows written to the T-MSIS submission file during the extract run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The extraction summary has been displayed and all provider records have been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program finalizes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Provider Master File and the T-MSIS Provider Submission output file are both closed, and the monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract process terminates successfully

all_rules.Rule_Name: File Closure and Process Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the extraction summary is reported, both the Provider Master File and the T-MSIS output file are closed, and the monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract process is completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The T-MSIS Provider Extract process is being initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must register its identity as 'PRVTMS01' — the monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract — so that all processing, logging, and output can be attributed to this specific extract program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Program as Monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system identifies itself as the monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract program (PRVTMS01) at the start of execution to establish the processing context for all subsequent operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The T-MSIS Provider Extract program (PRVTMS01) has been identified and is initializing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests the current date from the system calendar
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Today's date must be retrieved from the system calendar in Julian format (YYDDD) and stored internally for use throughout the extract process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Today's Date from System Calendar
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system retrieves the current date from the system calendar at program startup to establish the reference date for the T-MSIS submission period.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Today's date has been retrieved from the system calendar in Julian format (YYDDD)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The date is parsed and stored
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date must be stored as a 5-character Julian date where: the first 2 characters represent the 2-digit year (YY) stored as the current year identifier, and the last 3 characters represent the day-of-year (DDD) stored as the current day identifier — both components must be individually accessible for downstream comparisons and output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Date in Julian Format YYDDD
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system captures and stores today's date in Julian format, separating the 2-digit year and the 3-digit day-of-year components, to be used as the T-MSIS submission period identifier.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Today's date has been successfully captured and stored in Julian format (YYDDD) with the 2-digit year and 3-digit day-of-year components
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS Provider Extract process prepares output records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full 5-character Julian date (YYDDD) must be used as the T-MSIS Submission Period Identifier and must be populated in the reporting period field of every T-MSIS provider output record produced during this execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Julian Date Designated as T-MSIS Submission Period Identifier
all_rules.Rule_Description: The full Julian date (YYDDD) captured at program startup is designated as the T-MSIS Submission Period Identifier and must be stamped on every provider record written to the T-MSIS output file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The T-MSIS Provider extract process (PRVTMS01) is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the current date from the operating environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Today's date is captured and stored in Julian format (YYDDD), where the 5-character value represents a 2-digit year followed by a 3-digit day-of-year (e.g., 25143 = Year 25, Day 143), and this value is made available for enrollment year and day-of-year comparisons

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Today's Date in Julian Format for Enrollment Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system obtains today's date in Julian format (YYDDD), where the first two digits represent the 2-digit year and the last three digits represent the day-of-year. This date is used as the reference point for all subsequent enrollment date validations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Today's date has been captured in Julian format (YYDDD) as a 5-character value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system decomposes the Julian date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first 2 characters (positions 1–2) of the Julian date are extracted and stored as the Current Year (YY) component (e.g., from '25143', the value '25' is stored as the current year for use in enrollment year comparison)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Current Year Component from Julian Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system isolates the 2-digit year portion from the 5-character Julian date by reading the first two characters. This current year value is stored separately and used to detect future enrollment effective dates on provider records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Today's date has been captured in Julian format (YYDDD) as a 5-character value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system decomposes the Julian date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The last 3 characters (positions 3–5) of the Julian date are extracted and stored as the Current Day-of-Year (DDD) component (e.g., from '25143', the value '143' is stored as the current day-of-year for use in enrollment period validation)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Current Day-of-Year Component from Julian Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system isolates the 3-digit day-of-year portion from the 5-character Julian date by reading the last three characters. This day-of-year value is stored separately and is available for enrollment age or period-based validations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The 2-digit current year (YY) has been extracted from today's Julian date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the current year component
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 2-digit current year value (YY) is stored and remains available throughout the entire provider record processing loop, so that each active provider's enrollment effective year can be compared against it to detect future enrollment dates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Current Year for Provider Enrollment Year Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: The extracted 2-digit current year (YY) is retained in the system's working storage so that it can be compared against the enrollment effective year on each active provider record to identify future-dated enrollments.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The 3-digit current day-of-year (DDD) has been extracted from today's Julian date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the day-of-year component
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 3-digit day-of-year value (DDD) is stored and remains available throughout the entire provider record processing loop, so that the full Julian date (YYDDD) can be used to populate the Reporting Period field on each T-MSIS output record written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Current Day-of-Year for Enrollment Period Stamping
all_rules.Rule_Description: The extracted 3-digit day-of-year (DDD) is retained in the system's working storage. Together with the current year (YY), the full Julian date (YYDDD) is used to stamp the reporting period on every T-MSIS provider output record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Provider Master File sequential read process is about to begin
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the Provider Master File read loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to 'N' (Not Reached), indicating that provider records are available and processing should continue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Provider File Processing State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before reading any provider records, the system must initialize the processing state to indicate that records are still available for processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Provider Master File is open for input and the End-of-File flag is set to 'Not Reached'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the next record from the Provider Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next sequential provider record is retrieved from the Provider Master File and made available for processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Provider Record Sequentially
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must read provider records one at a time in sequential order from the Provider Master File to ensure every provider record is evaluated for T-MSIS reporting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read attempt has been made on the Provider Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the file status returned after the read operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status indicates End-of-File (no more records exist), the system marks all records as processed and exits the read loop; if the file status indicates a record was successfully retrieved, the provider record is made available for further processing and the loop continues

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect End of Provider Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each read attempt from the Provider Master File, the system must check whether all records have been processed to determine if the read loop should continue or terminate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read attempt on the Provider Master File has returned an End-of-File condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects that no more provider records are available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to TRUE, signaling that all provider records have been processed and the sequential read loop should terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark All Provider Records as Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no more provider records exist in the Provider Master File, the system must formally mark the processing as complete to stop further read attempts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read attempt on the Provider Master File has successfully retrieved a provider record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the record is available (no End-of-File condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The retrieved provider record is made available for downstream business processing, and the system loops back to read the next record after processing is complete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Processing Available Provider Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a provider record is successfully retrieved from the Provider Master File, it must be passed forward for business evaluation and potential inclusion in the T-MSIS output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provider's status in the Provider Master File is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the provider status is marked as Active, the provider record is selected and processed for T-MSIS extraction; if the provider status is not marked as Active, the provider record is skipped and no further action is taken for that record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Active Provider Selection for T-MSIS Extraction
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether a provider record from the Provider Master File should be included in the T-MSIS extract based on the provider's active status. Only providers with an Active status are selected for further processing and output; all others are skipped.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and its status has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provider's status is confirmed as Active
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider record is selected and passed to the T-MSIS row writing process, where it will be written to the T-MSIS output file and counted toward the total output record count

all_rules.Rule_Name: Include Active Provider in T-MSIS Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a provider record is confirmed as Active, it is forwarded to the T-MSIS output writing process. This ensures that only Active providers contribute to the T-MSIS provider extract file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and its status has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provider's status is not marked as Active
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider record is skipped entirely — no T-MSIS output record is created, no warning message is generated, and the output record counter is not incremented; processing continues with the next provider record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exclude Inactive Provider from T-MSIS Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a provider record is identified as not Active, it is entirely excluded from the T-MSIS extract. No output record is created, no warning is issued, and the record count is not incremented for inactive providers.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and contains a valid Effective Enrollment Date field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the provider record for T-MSIS output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts characters at positions 3 and 4 of the Provider Effective Enrollment Date field as the 2-digit enrollment year (WS-ENROLL-YY) for use in the future-year validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Enrollment Year from Provider Effective Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system extracts the 2-digit year component from the provider's enrollment effective date field to enable comparison against the current year for future-enrollment detection.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has started and accepted today's Julian date (YYDDD format) from the system
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The enrollment year validation is performed for an active provider record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system uses the 2-digit year (WS-TODAY-YY) extracted from positions 1 and 2 of today's Julian date as the reference current year for comparison against the provider's enrollment year

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current Year for Enrollment Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system uses the 2-digit current year that was captured from the system Julian date at program startup as the reference year for validating provider enrollment dates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The 2-digit enrollment year (WS-ENROLL-YY) has been extracted from the provider's Effective Enrollment Date, and the 2-digit current year (WS-TODAY-YY) is available from the system date captured at program start
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the provider's enrollment year is greater than the current year
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the provider's enrollment year (WS-ENROLL-YY) is strictly greater than the current year (WS-TODAY-YY), the provider record is identified as a potential future enrollment and a warning alert is triggered; otherwise, the record proceeds directly to provider data mapping without any warning

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Future Enrollment Year
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the provider's enrollment effective year against the current year to identify providers whose enrollment year appears to be dated in the future, which may indicate a data quality issue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has been evaluated and its enrollment effective year (WS-ENROLL-YY) is greater than the current year (WS-TODAY-YY)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The future enrollment condition is confirmed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the warning message 'PRVTMS01: FUTURE ENROLLMENT? NPI' followed by the provider's NPI (PRV-NPI) from the Provider Master Record to identify the specific provider with the suspect enrollment date; the provider record continues to be processed and written to the T-MSIS output file regardless of this warning

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Future Enrollment Warning Alert
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a provider's enrollment year is detected as being in the future, the system issues a warning message identifying the specific provider by their National Provider Identifier (NPI) to alert business users of a potential data quality issue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has been selected from the Provider Master File, and the current 2-digit year has been derived from today's Julian date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The 2-digit year extracted from positions 3-4 of the provider's Enrollment Effective Date is compared against the current 2-digit year
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the provider's enrollment effective year is greater than the current year, a warning message is displayed in the format 'PRVTMS01: FUTURE ENROLLMENT? NPI [Provider NPI]' to flag the record as a potential data quality issue; if the enrollment effective year is less than or equal to the current year, no warning is issued; in both cases, processing continues to write the provider record to the T-MSIS output file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Provider Future Enrollment Year Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing an active provider record for T-MSIS reporting, the system checks whether the provider's enrollment effective year is greater than the current year. If so, a warning message is displayed identifying the provider's NPI as a potential data quality issue. Processing continues regardless of the outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has been retrieved from the Provider Master File and a T-MSIS output record is being constructed for that provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS output record is being populated with provider details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Medicaid ID value from the Provider Master record must be copied exactly as-is into the Provider Identifier field of the T-MSIS output record, with no transformation or modification applied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Provider Medicaid ID to T-MSIS Provider Identifier Mapping
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building a T-MSIS output record for an active provider, the provider's Medicaid ID from the Provider Master record must be copied directly into the Provider Identifier field of the T-MSIS output record, establishing the authoritative provider identity in the T-MSIS submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and the provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) is present in the Provider Master record (PRV-NPI field)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS output record is being constructed for the qualifying active provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) value is copied exactly as-is from the Provider Master record (PRV-NPI) into the NPI field of the T-MSIS output record (WS-T-NPI), with no modification or transformation applied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Provider NPI Mapping to T-MSIS Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When building the T-MSIS output record for an active provider, the provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) must be sourced directly from the Provider Master record and mapped into the corresponding NPI field of the T-MSIS output record without transformation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and has passed the Active provider filter (i.e., the provider is marked as Active in the Provider Master File)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS output record is being constructed for the qualifying provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Provider Status field in the T-MSIS output record must be set to the value 'A', representing Active status, regardless of any other attributes of the provider record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Active Status Assignment for T-MSIS Provider Extract
all_rules.Rule_Description: For every provider record that has passed the Active status filter and is being extracted to the T-MSIS output file, the Provider Status field in the output record must be hardcoded to 'A' (Active). This ensures that all providers included in the T-MSIS extract are uniformly identified as Active, reflecting their eligibility status at the time of extraction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The monthly T-MSIS Provider Extract process has been initiated and the program has captured today's date in Julian format (YYDDD, where YY is the 2-digit year and DDD is the 3-digit day-of-year) at program initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A provider record is being prepared for writing to the T-MSIS output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Julian date value (YYDDD) that was captured at program startup is retrieved and made available to populate the T-MSIS output record's reporting period field, ensuring all records in the same extraction run share the identical submission period date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Submission Period Source Identification
all_rules.Rule_Description: The reporting period used for the T-MSIS monthly CMS submission is sourced from the Julian date captured once at program startup, ensuring all records in a single run share the same consistent submission period identifier.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has passed all validations and is ready to be written to the T-MSIS Provider Submission output file, and today's Julian date in YYDDD format (2-digit year followed by 3-digit day-of-year) is available from program initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS output record is being assembled for the active provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The T-MSIS output record's reporting period field (WS-T-PERIOD-YYDD) is populated with today's Julian date in YYDDD format, so that the record is correctly tagged with the monthly CMS submission period for that extraction run

all_rules.Rule_Name: T-MSIS Reporting Period Field Population with Julian Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: For every active provider record written to the T-MSIS submission file, the reporting period field must be populated with today's Julian date in YYDDD format to identify the monthly CMS submission period.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The T-MSIS output record's reporting period field has been populated with today's Julian date in YYDDD format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS Provider Submission output file is reviewed or processed by CMS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reporting period field value (YYDDD) uniquely identifies the monthly submission period for CMS, associating every provider record in the file with the correct reporting month and year of the T-MSIS submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Submission Period as Monthly CMS Identifier
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Julian date (YYDDD) stored in the T-MSIS output record's reporting period field serves as the official monthly submission period identifier for CMS, linking each extracted provider record to the specific reporting month in which it was submitted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A T-MSIS provider output record is being assembled for an active provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS detail structure is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record type identifier field in the T-MSIS detail structure must be set to the value 'PRV01'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Record Type Identifier to T-MSIS Provider Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When assembling a T-MSIS provider output record, the record type identifier must be set to 'PRV01' to classify the record as a provider submission within the T-MSIS reporting structure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and contains a Medicaid ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS provider output record is being assembled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Provider Medicaid ID from the Provider Master Record must be placed into the T-MSIS Provider ID field of the output record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate T-MSIS Provider ID from Medicaid ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The provider's Medicaid ID from the Provider Master File must be mapped to the Provider ID field in the T-MSIS output record to uniquely identify the provider in the T-MSIS submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and contains an NPI
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS provider output record is being assembled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The NPI from the Provider Master Record must be placed into the T-MSIS NPI field of the output record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate T-MSIS NPI from Provider Master NPI
all_rules.Rule_Description: The provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) from the Provider Master File must be mapped to the NPI field in the T-MSIS output record to support federal provider identification requirements.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has passed the active provider filter and is being written to the T-MSIS output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS provider output record is being assembled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The T-MSIS Status field must be hardcoded to the value 'A' representing Active status, regardless of any other status values present in the source record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set T-MSIS Provider Status to Active
all_rules.Rule_Description: All providers written to the T-MSIS output file are assigned a status of 'A' (Active), reflecting that only active providers from the Provider Master File are included in the T-MSIS submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current Julian date (YYDDD format) has been captured at program start, where YY represents the 2-digit current year and DDD represents the 3-digit day of the year
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS provider output record is being assembled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The T-MSIS Submission Period field must be populated with today's Julian date in YYDDD format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set T-MSIS Submission Period to Current Julian Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: The T-MSIS submission period field must reflect the current processing date in Julian format (YYDDD), where YY is the 2-digit year and DDD is the 3-digit day of the year, to indicate when the provider data was submitted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All required T-MSIS provider fields have been populated in the T-MSIS detail working storage structure, including record type 'PRV01', Provider Medicaid ID, NPI, status 'A', and Julian date submission period
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS provider output record assembly is finalized
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The fully populated T-MSIS detail structure must be consolidated and moved into the T-MSIS output record, making it ready to be written to the T-MSIS output file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Consolidate All Fields into Complete T-MSIS Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all individual fields (record type 'PRV01', Provider Medicaid ID, NPI, Active status 'A', and Julian submission period) have been populated in the T-MSIS detail structure, the complete structure must be moved into the T-MSIS output record before writing to the T-MSIS output file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record has been selected from the Provider Master File and all T-MSIS output fields have been populated: Provider Medicaid ID, NPI, Status set to 'A' (Active), and Reporting Period set to today's Julian date (YYDDD format)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fully assembled T-MSIS provider detail record is transferred into the T-MSIS output record structure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The T-MSIS output record structure contains the complete provider detail ready for submission, with all fields accurately reflecting the source provider master data and the current reporting period

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assemble and Write Active Provider Record to T-MSIS Submission File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an active provider record has been fully prepared with all required T-MSIS fields (Medicaid ID, NPI, Active status, and reporting period), the assembled detail is transferred into the T-MSIS output record structure before being written to the monthly CMS T-MSIS Provider Submission file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The T-MSIS output record structure has been fully populated with the active provider's Medicaid ID, NPI, Active status ('A'), and today's Julian date as the reporting period
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The T-MSIS output record is written to the monthly CMS T-MSIS Provider Submission file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider record is successfully appended to the T-MSIS Provider Submission output file, and the total count of T-MSIS provider rows written is incremented by 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Formatted Provider Record to Monthly CMS T-MSIS Provider Submission File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the T-MSIS output record structure is fully populated, the provider record is physically written to the monthly CMS T-MSIS Provider Submission output file and the total output record count is incremented by one.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active provider record from the Provider Master File has been processed and all required T-MSIS output fields have been populated (Provider Medicaid ID, NPI, Status set to 'A', and Reporting Period set to today's Julian date)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provider record is successfully written to the T-MSIS output file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The running T-MSIS provider record counter is incremented by exactly 1, and the updated count reflects the total number of provider records successfully written to the T-MSIS output file during the current execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: T-MSIS Provider Record Count Tracking
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each time an active provider record is successfully written to the T-MSIS output file, a running counter is incremented by 1 to track the total number of provider records extracted. This count is reported at the end of the process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All records in the Provider Master File have been processed and the T-MSIS extraction run is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The extraction process reaches its completion point after writing all qualifying active provider records to the T-MSIS submission file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays a summary message identified by program name 'PRVTMS01' showing the label 'T-MSIS PROVIDER ROWS=' followed by the final total count (WS-OUT-COUNT) of provider records successfully written to the T-MSIS submission file during the extraction run

all_rules.Rule_Name: T-MSIS Provider Extraction Summary Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon completion of processing all provider records from the Provider Master File, the system reports the total number of active provider records successfully written to the T-MSIS submission file as a final extraction summary.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All records in the Provider Master File have been read and processed, and eligible active provider records have been written to the T-MSIS Provider Submission Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The monthly provider extract process reaches completion after exhausting all Provider Master File records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'PRVTMS01: T-MSIS PROVIDER ROWS=' followed by the total count of provider rows written to the T-MSIS Provider Submission Output File during the current extract run

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Total T-MSIS Provider Records Written
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all provider records from the Provider Master File have been processed, the total number of provider rows successfully written to the T-MSIS Provider Submission Output File is displayed as a final summary of the monthly extract run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All provider records have been processed, eligible active provider records have been written to the T-MSIS Provider Submission Output File, and the total output record count has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The monthly provider extract process is ready to terminate
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Provider Master Input File is closed first, followed by the closure of the T-MSIS Provider Submission Output File, and the monthly provider extract process ends successfully

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Provider Master Input File and T-MSIS Output File at Process Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon completion of all provider record processing and after displaying the final record count, both the Provider Master Input File and the T-MSIS Provider Submission Output File must be formally closed to finalize the monthly provider extract process.

description:
PRVTMS01 is a batch program that extracts active Medicaid providers from the Provider Master File and writes them into the monthly CMS T-MSIS (Transformed Medicaid Statistical Information System) Provider Submission File (PEM-10). For each active provider record, it populates a T-MSIS detail row containing the provider's Medicaid ID, NPI, active status, and current reporting period, then counts and displays the total number of records written.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM (Indexed), Sequential File - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Capture the current date as the reporting period date in Julian format (YYDDD with 2-digit year) to be used as the T-MSIS submission period identifier 2: Julian Date Decomposition - Break down today's Julian date into its year component (YY) and day-of-year component (DDD) for use in enrollment age validation 3: Provider Master File Sequential Read - Read all provider records sequentially from the Provider Master file one at a time until all records are processed 4: Active Provider Filtering - Evaluate each provider record and select only those providers whose status is marked as Active; skip all inactive providers 5: Enrollment Date Future-Year Validation - Extract the 2-digit year from the provider's effective (enrollment) date and compare it against the current year to detect providers whose enrollment year appears to be in the future 6: Future Enrollment Alert - Display a warning message identifying the NPI of any provider whose enrollment year is greater than the current year, flagging potential data quality issues 7: Provider Medicaid ID Mapping - Copy the provider's Medicaid ID from the Provider Master record into the T-MSIS output record as the provider identifier field 8: Provider NPI Mapping - Copy the provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) from the Provider Master record into the T-MSIS output record 9: Provider Active Status Assignment - Set the provider status field in the T-MSIS output record to 'A' (Active) for all providers being extracted 10: Submission Period Assignment - Populate the T-MSIS output record's reporting period field with today's Julian date (YYDDD), identifying the monthly submission period for CMS 11: T-MSIS Record Formatting - Assemble the complete T-MSIS provider output record with record type identifier 'PRV01', provider ID, NPI, status, and submission period 12: T-MSIS Output Record Writing - Write the formatted provider record to the monthly CMS T-MSIS Provider Submission output file 13: Extracted Record Count Tracking - Increment a running counter each time a provider record is successfully written to the T-MSIS output file 14: Extraction Summary Reporting - Display the total number of provider rows written to the T-MSIS submission file upon completion of the extraction process 15: File Closure and Process Completion - Close the Provider Master input file and the T-MSIS output file and end the monthly provider extract process
